lines.narration: In the empty garage Twinkie, the friend in the mint-green shirt, won't hear the leave-town plan — and he lays it out plainly: the trouble Sean has made doesn't stop at Takashi, it runs all the way up to Kamata now.

claim.subject: the friend in the mint-green shirt

lines.narration: Sean says it quietly: he's going to go talk to Kamata himself. Twinkie stares at him like he's lost his mind — Han is gone, you can't just walk into Kamata's place. And Sean's answer stops the argument cold: that's all I've got.

claim.subject: the young man in the white thermal shirt

lines.narration: So Twinkie goes to his green car, runs a hand along the panel, and pries open a hidden stash in the quarter.

claim.subject: the friend in the mint-green shirt

lines.narration: He shoves a battered leather satchel at Sean — something Han would have wanted him to have — a thick wad of banknotes to buy his way through Kamata's door alive. Sean asks if he needs it. He'll figure it out.

claim.subject: the friend in the mint-green shirt

lines.narration: Night, dark clothes, a narrow alley packed with men in embroidered gang jackets — one of them carrying a bat — and the crowd closing behind him as he walks to the guarded door and asks for Mr Kamata.

claim.subject: the young man in the white thermal shirt

lines.narration: He opens the bag in the doorway. A bald elder looks in, goes still — and that is the whole password. They walk him inside, past the Fuji print, into a warm lantern-lit lounge where every head turns to track the gaijin coming through.

claim.subject: the young man in the white thermal shirt

lines.narration: Takashi gets nose to nose with him first. Sean doesn't flinch — I didn't come here to see you — and Kamata-san has something to give you. The bag is carried forward and lifted open at the old man's table.

claim.subject: the young man in the white thermal shirt

lines.narration: Then Sean says it to Kamata's face. He's only returning what was his in the first place. That's not why he came — he came to apologize, because he and Takashi have embarrassed themselves badly in front of this man.

claim.subject: the young man in the white thermal shirt

lines.narration: Takashi cuts in — don't listen to this gaijin — and throws it back at the old man: after everything you've done, you're giving me orders? Kamata just shuts his eyes over the cigar and lets him hang himself.
And then the old man doesn't say a word. He just stares, and Takashi's defiance folds — the nephew drops his head into a bow. One look does what no shouting could.

claim.subject: the older man with the cigar

lines.narration: Sean lays out his peaceful solution. A race — he and Takashi settle it once and for all, and the loser leaves Tokyo for good. Takashi sneers that he's already beaten him once. Kamata weighs it over the cigar, and says one word. Good.

claim.subject: the young man in the white thermal shirt

lines.narration: The terms are brutally simple, and they cut both ways: win and Takashi is gone — lose and Sean leaves the only place he's got left.

Now the crew builds. They rebuild the striped Mustang around the Nissan twin-cam engine — a turbo swings down on the hoist, welders throw sparks under the lifted body, Earl in the plaid shirt lifting an injector to the light.
And out on the mountain Sean runs the stripped car, learning the drift — the Mustang breaking loose onto dirt and throwing a wall of dust through the hillside turns, over and over.

At the roadside the warning lands. DK picked this road for a reason — it's his mountain, and he's the only one who has ever made it to the bottom. Sean's reply hardens into a frown, and he turns to stare off down the road.

claim.subject: the young man in the black durag

lines.narration: Race night. The crowd lines the ledge above the floodlit dam, and then every head turns one way at once: Kamata arrives with his minders, and the people part to let him take his place.

claim.subject: the older man with the cigar

lines.narration: Sean sits behind the wheel with his eyes shut, breathing himself calm, Takashi flat-faced beside him in the black coupe. The starter throws both arms up — and drops them. Both cars launch into the downhill dark.

claim.subject: the bald man in the dark suit
